purpose: Construir un juego web liviano click-to-walk y fusionarlo con los mundos pseudo/real-3D de Spaces/Rail World sin convertir la cámara en un dron difícil de controlar.
important_ideas: Image-first room engine: art provides most visual complexity; code makes the world inhabitable.
Pinterest/reference corpus is discovery material, not automatic production assets.
Asset qualification must be role-specific: alpha/cutout requirements for sprites, opaque images allowed for backgrounds/textures.
Human should not curate 100 images manually; discovery, rejection, cutout validation, composition and QA should be automated.
Click moves avatar; camera is composition assistance, not a permanently free vehicle.
Camera lineage converged on turn handoff: approach the avatar's turn hinge before rotating toward the new route.
decisions: No direct Pinterest hotlinks/assets in final runtime by default.
No rectangular source-photo boundaries in avatar pieces.
No mouse-drag free camera rotation/movement for normal navigation.
Camera may catch up when avatar leaves a comfortable composition zone.
At a route turn, camera must travel to the prior avatar/hinge position and wait for avatar proximity before rotating.
Visual changes require deterministic browser screenshots and AI self-critique before delivery.

verification: Walk World browser review + public route verification.
Rail World V7/V8/V9/V10 GitHub Actions browser tests.
V10 verifies camera travels forward before turn and rotates near the turn handoff.
learnings: A visually correct route can still feel wrong if camera orientation is changed from a stale/distant camera position.
Movement geometry and camera choreography must share explicit hinge points.
Screenshot evidence catches obvious composition failures earlier than user-supplied screenshots.
alternatives: Pre-rendered depth-frame rail was explored as a cheap alternative to live Spaces rendering, then superseded when a more advanced live Rail World runtime was recovered.
V7 permanent-ish autofollow was refined into composition states in V8 and path-turn/handoff behavior in V9/V10.
unresolved: Human acceptance of V10 camera feel remains distinct from CI success.
Generalize camera turn-handoff into reusable world-engine knowledge rather than leaving it only inside one demo.
Generalize role-specific asset qualification into a reusable build tool.

findings.text: Camera turns must hand off at the avatar/route hinge, not rotate from a stale distant camera position.
Pinterest/reference discovery is not automatic production-asset authority; final sprites require role-specific qualification.
Deterministic browser screenshots and self-critique belong before visual delivery, not after user reports an obvious defect.
